scope: One-operation capability guidance through the installed Agent entry; no new permission dimension, Provider, SDK, browser patch, account workflow, release or deployment.

D1.evidence: The canonical static definition drives Core shape validation, MCP conditional schema and help; all first-batch operations and the missing-session/origin/file_refs counterexamples pass Core and schema self-checks.

D2.evidence: Core distinguishes visible Profile metadata from target-operation authorization; invisible Profiles stop before Harbor. Both profile.read and exact profile.list use the existing Grant/Profile/task owner intersection.

D3.evidence: Core, Harbor and Plugin tests distinguish defined, unknown, out_of_scope, not_exposed, limited, denied, human_control, stopped, stale and unknown states.

D4.evidence: Harbor's existing control owner remains authoritative; static guidance stays readable and human_control wins over weaker Page uncertainty without inventing a restriction for control_owner=none.

D5.evidence: After a successful description, stop and human takeover make the subsequent execution fail/not_dispatched; fresh Grant, visibility, target authorization, policy and Harbor facts are rechecked before return and again during execution.

D6.evidence: Plugin tests prove describe branches before ensureRuntime. Installed before/after snapshots for both Providers and after restart showed unchanged Run, authorization-decision, lease, session, browser-process and Runtime-service counts.

D7.evidence: Desktop client tests cover describe against an old Runtime and discovery definition/response mismatch. Installed auxiliary checks cover package assets, startup and general version refusal. The formal package reports the frozen workspace identity; an explicit stop/start changed runtime_id and both Provider descriptions reread persisted facts.

D8.evidence: The same installed client and public operation definition described camoufox and chrome_official as supported/allowed/no_known_blocker, then each completed instance.start, instance.observe, original-Run query and instance.stop on one local non-sensitive page.

D9.evidence: A short Codex Agent used only the installed MCP: connect, contextual describe for instance.input, start, observe/snapshot, one text input, query the original input Run, and stop. The input Run and query both returned succeeded; no execution retry occurred.
